title: Cap. VI Arg. 5: Arminian foresight — certainty only from God intuiting, not specially causing
pass_a_gloss: But in that Arminian Predestination, where foresighted faith draws election after itself, there is no certainty of salvation from God specially causing, but only from God intuiting. For in the four decrees of Arminius, by which he describes the nature of predestination, there is none that brings certainty of salvation to any singular person, by way of a cause infallibly operating; but he leaves the salvation of the elect certain to God by way of one intuiting.
pass_b_english: In Arminian predestination, where foresighted faith drags election after it, there is no certainty of salvation from God as special cause — only from God as onlooker. Of Arminius's four decrees describing predestination, none gives any singular person certainty of salvation by an infallibly operating cause; elect salvation stays certain to God only as one who sees.
source_text: At in illa Praedestinatione Arminiana, ubi fides praevisa post se trahit electionem, nulla est certitudo salutis ex Deo specialiter causante, sed solummodo ex Deo intuente. Nam in quatuor Arminii decretis, quibus praedestinationis naturam describit, nullum est quod certitudinem salutis singulari alicui personae apportet, per modum causae infallibiliter operantis; sed salutem electorum Deo certam relinquit per modum intuentis.
